Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-09
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Rao (VeraHealth CTO), Ethan Brown (Lead ML Eng), Sara Lopez (SRE)

Summary (auto): quick review of weekly POC benchmarks vs baseline provider; discussed latency and throughput numbers, tuning steps (batching, KV cache, quantization), next steps for dedicated pilot and VPC networking follow-up.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Patel: ok hey everyone thanks for joining for the weekly POC sync, I think Maya has the updated numbers to walk through, real quick: we looked at baseline provider numbers and our Redwood infra numbers across the same model and prompt set, did i miss anyone on the attendee list?
[00:12] Dr. Priya: no, all good, thanks Jordan, and thanks for the follow-up, we've been eager to see the numbers for higher context lengths this week
[00:22] Maya Chen: yeah cool, i'll share my screen after i talk through, apologies if the transcript shuffles some things, audio was a little fuzz at the start, but the key takeaways: for the 2k context gen workload, redwood hosted (optimized stack) p50 ~120ms, p95 ~540ms, throughput ~125 tokens/sec; baseline provider p50 ~210ms, p95 ~1.2s, throughput ~70 tokens/sec. those are med-quality transcribed metrics, caveat that provider used slightly different batching defaults unless we forced parity
[01:05] Ethan Brown: wait so that's almost half the p95 of baseline, is that with KV cache enabled?
[01:11] Maya Chen: good call - for the 2k tests KV cache was enabled for both, where parity mattered was batching: we forced baseline to single-request batching but they had a lower batch cap; on Redwood we used dynamic batching with a 64-token batch target which improved throughput and P95.
[01:35] Sara Lopez: what about the 8k context runs? our main concern is the 8k LLM for long patient notes
[01:42] Maya Chen: 8k was trickier, numbers are: Redwood p50 ~420ms, p95 ~1.6s, throughput ~60 tokens/sec; baseline p50 ~820ms, p95 ~3.8s, throughput ~28 tokens/sec. Redwood benefited from KV prefetch and chunked cache; baseline fell off without larger KV cache quotas. again, transcript may swap some model names but numbers are roughly correct
[02:12] Dr. Priya: those numbers look promising, our SLA for interactive UX is p95 <1s in most flows, but we can accept longer for batch backfill. how do we get p95 down under 1s for 8k?
[02:25] Maya Chen: two paths: 1) tuning on hosted: increase batch target + reduce tail latency via smaller kernel variants OR 2) move to Dedicated capacity where we can pin larger GPU instances and enable throughput-focused kernels and higher CPU->GPU IO bandwidth. The Dedicated 4xA100 config we prototyped drops 8k p95 to ~920ms in our lab tests (quantized x8/bit).
[02:52] Ethan Brown: quantized x8? does that impact our accuracy/regression risk? we run a clinical summarization prompt set, small hallucination risk is unacceptable
[03:01] Maya Chen: correct, quantization can shift outputs slightly. our recommendation is to run a small eval set (your clinical prompts) against quantized variants; Redwood Optimize can generate per-prompt delta scores and flag regressions. in our experiments the top-1 accuracy delta was <0.6% for the summarization prompts we used, but your prompt set might differ
[03:24] Jordan Patel: calling out compliance: VeraHealth, you mentioned SOC2 and data residency earlier. for Dedicated we support VPC and KMS integration — that means audit logs and customer-managed keys, is that a hard requirement for the pilot?
[03:36] Dr. Priya: for the pilot, we can operate on hosted but must validate encryption at rest and audit trails. for production, yes we need VPC and customer KMS.
[03:44] Jordan Patel: got it, we'll include the VPC deep-dive as a follow-up.
[03:48] Maya Chen: back to perf, there's one more config we tried: persistent KV cache on Dedicated reduced the p95 tail by ~25% in steady-state for long context flows. Also enabling token-level caching for repeated prefixes improved throughput by 1.4x on our sample workload.
[04:08] Ethan Brown: nice, can you share the benchmark spreadsheet with the raw numbers (p50/p95/tokens-per-sec and batch sizes)?
[04:15] Maya Chen: yes, i'll upload the spreadsheet after the call — note column for 'parity tweaks' where we documented batching caps and kernel variant.
[04:23] Sara Lopez: any notes about cost? baseline pricing was attractive but lower perf, what's the delta if we go dedicated with redwood vs continue with baseline hosted?
[04:33] Jordan Patel: quick ballpark: baseline hosted for your current volume roughly $X/day (we'll provide exact numbers) vs Redwood Dedicated 4-GPU committed price is higher per month but gives predictable latency and lower per-token unit cost at scale. I'll send a side-by-side TCO that includes burst pricing and caching savings.
[04:52] Dr. Priya: good, and what about failover — if Dedicated capacity has an outage, can requests fallback to hosted?
[04:58] Maya Chen: yes, we support smart routing and fallback policies; you can set priority rules to route to dedicated first and fall back to hosted replicas or a cheaper model variant. this is how we keep SLAs without over-committing capacity.
[05:14] Ethan Brown: one more ask - can we run a short 48-hour soak with our synthetic traffic shape? that would give us more realistic tails
[05:20] Jordan Patel: absolutely, we can set up a soak on a dedicated pilot window — need to confirm dates and sizing.
[05:26] Maya Chen: actionables: i'll re-run the 8k with dynamic batching and bigger KV quota, attach raw logs; Jordan will produce pricing; Ethan to share traffic histogram.
[05:35] Dr. Priya: sounds good. Also, can you annotate the benchmark spreadsheet with which runs used quantization vs full-precision so our clinical team can evaluate output diffs?
[05:45] Maya Chen: yes will include quant vs fp columns and example diffs.
[05:49] Jordan Patel: ok final recap: Maya shares spreadsheet by Wed, Jordan sends dedicated pricing by Thu, VeraHealth provides traffic hist by Fri, schedule VPC deep-dive for next week. thanks everyone.
[05:59] Dr. Priya: thanks all.
[06:02] Ethan Brown: thanks, bye.
[06:05] Sara Lopez: bye.
